description: The line plot illustrates the training loss over steps for various model architectures and sizes, using a dataset of 20 million samples. The x-axis represents the number of training steps, ranging from 0k to 440k, with major tick marks at intervals of 20k. The y-axis shows the training loss, scaled from 0.0 to 0.85, with gridlines at 0.2, 0.4, and 0.6. Six distinct models are compared: ChemBART Small 20M (red), ChemBART Medium 20M (blue), ChemBERTa Small 20M (green), ChemBERTa Medium 20M (orange), ChemLLaMA Small 20M (purple), and ChemLLaMA Medium 20M (brown). All models begin with high training loss near 0.8 at step 0k, and all exhibit a rapid initial decline in loss. The ChemBERTa Small 20M model (green) shows the steepest initial drop, reaching a loss of approximately 0.15 by 440k steps. The ChemLLaMA Medium 20M model (brown) demonstrates the best performance, achieving the lowest loss of all models, stabilizing at approximately 0.01 by 440k steps. The ChemBART Small 20M model (red) declines more slowly, stabilizing at around 0.25 at 440k steps. The ChemLLaMA Small 20M model (purple) and ChemBERTa Medium 20M model (orange) follow similar trends, with losses stabilizing around 0.15 to 0.20. The ChemBART Medium 20M model (blue) shows a slightly higher loss than the ChemLLaMA Medium 20M model, stabilizing around 0.05. The plot includes a zoomed-in section from 420k to 440k steps to highlight the final loss values.
caption_used: Training Loss vs. Steps for Each Model Type by Model Size with a Data Size of 20 million. The loss trends for 10 million and 20 million datasets are similar. The ChemBERTa Small 20M model exhibits the steepest decline in training loss, reaching approximately 0.15 at 440k steps. ChemLLaMA Medium 20M consistently outperforms ChemBART Medium 20M, achieving the lowest loss of all models at 0.01. The ChemBART Small 20M model shows a slower rate of decline compared to ChemLLaMA Small 20M, stabilizing at around 0.25 at 440k steps.
